To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
(a) interviewers' decisions are highly variable; (b) interviewers' decision rules are highly variable; and (c) the interviewers' decision rule is a function of the interviewer's personality.
(a) interviewers do not make consistent decisions and (b) interviewers' decisions are based on idiosyncratically defined job-relevant attributes.

(1) interviewers' selection decisions vary greatly across interviewers; (2) interviewers' decisions are idiosyncractic; (3) the idiosyncracy of interviewers' decisions jeopardizes the effectiveness of employment interviews; and (4) the effectiveness of employment interview can be enhanced by (a) training interviewers to be consistent and accurate and (b) training interviewees to perform well in the interview.
